---
title: "VG08 — Joint model with study and subject random intercepts on understood: children with Down syndrome"
abstract: "*VG08 extends VG07 by adding a non-centred subject-level random intercept on the understood trajectory. This partitions between-child variability from the within-child correlation induced by repeated observations and from residual Beta-Binomial overdispersion. The estimated between-subject SD is large enough to materially change the population-level trajectory.*"
---

## Overview

288 of the 510 unique DS subjects in the pooled dataset contribute more than one observation (maximum eight observations on a single subject). Treating those repeated observations as independent — as VG07 does — inflates the Beta-Binomial dispersion to absorb the within-subject correlation and biases the population trajectory toward observation density. VG08 separates the three sources of variability explicitly:

- Between-study variation (study-level random intercepts, as in VG07)
- Between-subject variation on the understood trajectory (new in VG08)
- Residual Beta-Binomial overdispersion (within-occasion measurement noise)

The model structure follows VG07 with one additional term on the understood logit:

$$f_U(a, s, i) = \text{intercept}_U + \text{slope}_U \cdot a_z + g_U(a) + \delta_U[s] + \delta^{\text{subj}}_U[i]$$
$$h(a, s) = \text{intercept}_q + \text{slope}_q \cdot a_z + g_q(a) + \delta_q[s]$$

with $\delta^{\text{subj}}_U[i] = \tau^{\text{subj}}_U \cdot z_i$, $z_i \sim \mathrm{Normal}(0, 1)$ (non-centred parameterisation), $\tau^{\text{subj}}_U \sim \mathrm{HalfNormal}(0.5)$. The production ratio retains the study-only RE structure from VG07 in this first iteration; VG09 adds the parallel subject RE on `q`.

## Results

### Variance partition

The structural change between VG07 and VG08 is the addition of the subject RE on $U$. The estimated study-level SD is essentially unchanged, while the Beta-Binomial dispersion parameter shifts substantially as the model reassigns within-subject correlation to its proper structural source:

| Variance component (logit-SD, understood) | VG07 | VG08 |
| :--- | ---: | ---: |
| Between-study ($\tau_U$) | 0.50 | 0.51 |
| Between-subject ($\tau^{\text{subj}}_U$) | — | **0.78** |
| Beta-Binomial dispersion $a_\kappa$ (mid-age log) | 1.75 | **2.93** |

The Beta-Binomial dispersion factor at mid-age jumps from $\exp(1.75) \approx 5.8$ to $\exp(2.93) \approx 18.6$ — residual overdispersion shrinks to about a third of the VG07 value. The same pattern appears on the spoken side ($a_{\kappa,S}: 1.40 \to 1.86$, $\kappa_{\min,S}: 2.51 \to 4.58$) even though no subject RE was added to the production ratio — cleaner $p_U$ propagates through $p_S = p_U \cdot q$.

The fact that the between-study SD is essentially unchanged is itself informative: VG07's study REs were not secretly absorbing within-subject correlation.

### Population trajectory

Median values (population-level trajectory; $\delta_U[s] = \delta^{\text{subj}}_U[i] = 0$), with 90% credible intervals:

| Age (months) | Understood (median) | Spoken (median) | Production ratio (q) |
| ---: | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 12 | 25 [16–34] | 0.5 [0.2–1.0] | 0.02 |
| 24 | 91 [68–115] | 13 [7–19] | 0.14 |
| 36 | 189 [148–231] | 57 [37–79] | 0.30 |
| 48 | 259 [207–311] | 163 [124–206] | 0.64 |
| 60 | 345 [283–408] | 272 [217–326] | 0.79 |
| 72 | 435 [362–506] | 361 [299–425] | 0.84 |
| 84 | 511 [417–601] | 398 [324–471] | 0.79 |

Compared with VG07, the VG08 trajectory:

- starts **lower** at 12–18 months (typical understood at 12 months drops from 41 to 25);
- rises **steeper** through the middle of the age range (12 → 60 months: 5× understood-vocabulary growth becomes 14×);
- ends **higher** at the top of the age range (~511 understood at 84 months vs ~423 in VG07);
- and the production ratio $q$ **plateaus** around 0.78–0.84 from ~60 months onwards rather than continuing to climb toward 1.0.

The mechanism is mechanical: under VG07 every observation contributes equally to the likelihood, so a subject with five observations exerts five times the influence of a singleton. The 288 multi-observation DS subjects contribute 78.8% of the rows but only 56.5% of the children — and because longitudinal recruitment tends to over-represent higher-engaging families, those multi-observation subjects also sit above the population mean. VG07's smooth trajectory therefore tracks observation density, not child frequency. VG08's subject REs absorb each subject's consistent deviation, so the population-level trajectory becomes "expected within-subject change as a typical DS child ages", which is the developmentally interesting quantity.

The production-ratio plateau caveat. The VG07 reading was that $q$ approaches 1.0 by the later school years — i.e. DS children eventually speak essentially every word they understand. The VG08 reading was that $q$ stalls at ~0.8 from about 60 months onward. **VG09 subsequently revises this reading again** (the plateau under VG08 turns out to be its own variant of the Simpson's-paradox issue, on the production-ratio side) — see [VG09](vg09.qmd).

### Subject-marginalised posterior predictive distribution

The population-level trajectory above answers *"how does a typical DS child's vocabulary change as they age?"*. For predictive intervals around an unseen DS child's word counts, we integrate over a freshly-sampled subject random intercept drawn from $\mathrm{Normal}(0, \tau^{\text{subj}}_U)$. The relevant figures and posterior-predictive summaries in `output/models/VG08-age-understood-spoken-ds-re-subj/` use this subject-marginalised distribution; the latent probability columns (`p_median`, `Ey_median`) describe the population-mean conditional probability and are unchanged.

### Diagnostics

VG08 sampled at rep quality (6 chains × 6 000 + 6 000 NUTS, target_accept = 0.95): r̂_max = 1.005, ESS_bulk_min = 1 663 across reported parameters, zero divergences, 26 m 39 s wall time. ESS_bulk for the population-level parameters comfortably exceeds 5 000.

## Status of VG08 in the family

VG08 was the headline DS joint model very briefly (within a single day, 13 May 2026) before VG09 superseded it. Its place in the report is methodological: it makes the variance-partition argument for the understood trajectory, and the K-fold leave-one-subject-out comparison ranks it cleanly between VG07 and VG09 (see the [model comparison chapter](model-comparison.qmd)). It is also the model that exposes the asymmetry that VG09 then fixes: between-subject variability on `q` is even larger than between-subject variability on `U`, and VG08 absorbs it into the spoken-side Beta-Binomial dispersion.

For full per-model output see `output/models/VG08-age-understood-spoken-ds-re-subj/index.html`.
